bhutan.title: Flag of the Kingdom of Bhutan

colors.note: Represents the secular authority of the king
Represents the Buddhist spiritual tradition, particularly the Drukpa Kagyu and Nyingma schools
The Druk (thunder dragon) representing the country and its purity

desc:
- Diagonally divided from hoist-bottom to fly-top into yellow (upper hoist) and orange (lower fly), with a white Druk (thunder dragon) clutching four jewels centred on the dividing line
- Introduced in 1949 and standardised in 1969 to its current proportions and dragon design
trivia:
- Druk means 'thunder dragon', and Bhutan's endonym Druk Yul translates as 'Land of the Thunder Dragon'
- The jewels (norbu) clutched in the dragon's claws represent the wealth and prosperity of the country
- Earlier versions of the flag showed a green dragon; the colour was changed to white in 1969 to symbolise purity
